Definition: to awe or (intransitive) to dread; hence, to harass
BiblicalUsage: The word means to be in awe, to dread, and by extension to be the thing that terrifies. Moses says fear not, for the Lord goes with you; Isaiah says let the Lord be your fear and your dread; Joshua is told to be strong and not afraid; and the spies' report had already taught Israel to dread the giants instead of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that dread has to go somewhere, and God means it to land on Him. Fear the Lord and you need not fear the enemy; fear the enemy and you will never enter the land.
